case_name: Rahul Builders v Arihant Fertilizers and Chemical and Another
respondent:
Arihant Fertilizers and Chemical and Another
Supreme Court of India

2 November 2007
Criminal Appeal No. 525 of 2005
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
1.  Failure on the part of the appellant to serve a proper notice strictly in terms of proviso appended to Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act (for short "the Act") whether would lead to quashing of a criminal proceedings initiated by II Additional Sessions Judge, Ne much on a complaint made by the appellant herein is the question involved in this appeal which arises out of a judgment and order dated 22.11.2004 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh in Misc. Criminal Case No. 2924 of 2004.
2.  Appellant is a partnership firm. Respondent No. 1 entered into a contract with it for construction of a building and factory premises. Appellant executed the said contract. It submitted bills for execution of contractual work for a sum of Rs. 26,46,647/-. Respondent No. 1 had made payments of Rs. 17,74,2
facts: The appellant, Rahul Builders, is a partnership firm that executed a contract with Respondent No. 1 to construct a building and factory premises.
Respondent No. 1 had made payments of Rs. 17,74,238/- and a balance of Rs. 8,72,409/- was said to be outstanding.
A cheque for a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- drawn on Federal Bank Limited, Indore was issued by Respondent No. 1 in favour of the appellant.
Upon presentation of the said cheque, it was not honoured on the ground that Respondent No. 1 had closed its account with the bank.
issues: Whether the notice issued by the appellant to Respondent No. 1 was valid under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
Whether the High Court erred in quashing the criminal proceedings against Respondent No. 1
petitioner_arguments: The notice issued by the appellant was not invalid, as it did not specify a particular period for payment
The demand made by the appellant was not vague, as it specified the amount due under the dishonoured cheque
respondent_arguments: The notice issued by the appellant was invalid, as it did not comply with the requirements of Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
The demand made by the appellant was vague, as it did not specify the amount due under the dishonoured cheque
court_reasoning: Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act does not speak of a 15 days' notice, but rather contemplates service of notice and payment of the amount of cheque within 15 days from the date of receipt thereof
The notice issued by the appellant was valid, as it made a demand for the payment of the said amount of money
holding: The High Court's decision to quash the criminal proceedings against Respondent No. 1 is set aside
The criminal proceedings pending against Respondent No. 1 are allowed to continue
cases_cited: Mr. Jain relied upon a decision of this Court in Suman Sethi v. Ajay K
On this aspect of the matter, we may consider K.R. Indira v. Dr. G
